title: How balance combines movement, vision and body signals
intro: Balance comes from cooperation between the inner ears, eyes, body-position sensors and brain. Dizziness is a symptom with many possible causes; understanding the system does not establish an ear diagnosis.

sections.heading: Turning movements
paragraphs: Fluid-filled semicircular canals detect changes in head rotation. Their sensory cells send messages to the brain; signals may briefly continue after spinning stops, which helps explain a playground sensation.

sections.heading: Gravity and straight movement
paragraphs: The otolith organs use tiny crystals and sensory cells to detect head tilt and linear acceleration. Normal crystals are part of the system; their presence alone is not a disease.

sections.heading: Combining information
paragraphs: The brain compares ear signals with vision and feedback from muscles and joints. It adjusts posture and eye movements, helping keep a sign readable while the head moves.

sections.heading: Everyday implications
paragraphs: Conflicting signals can cause motion sickness. Poor lighting, reduced sensation and some medicines increase fall risk. Sit safely during dizziness and avoid driving or climbing until assessed when appropriate.

sections.heading: When to seek help
paragraphs: Recurrent dizziness needs assessment, including medicines and other causes. Sudden dizziness with weakness, speech trouble, double vision or inability to walk needs emergency assessment, not a home repositioning experiment.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira feels less steady in darkness. She improves lighting and discusses vision, sensation and balance rather than blaming the ears alone.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben has new vertigo and slurred speech. His family seeks emergency help instead of trying online exercises.
